usual_baseline: Diagnosis and current medication are nearly always recorded (80–100%). Allergies (13–27.5%), user-friendly information or useful links (7.5–23%), copying in service users (3%), crisis planning (20%) and actions for the GP are the weak items. Timeliness is usually good: letters within 7 days 92–99%, within 14 days 95%.
fix_that_works: A letter template with recommended headings plus junior teaching: psychiatric diagnosis 83.5% to 97.1%, follow-up plan 80.2% to 98.6%, care coordinator 8.3% to 54.3% [3274]. At re-audit in one CAMHS clinic, medication indications rose 32.5% to 56.6% and risk assessment 70% to 86.6% [3246].
fix_that_fails: After the template, action for GP fell from 44.6% to 27.1% and medical comorbidity stayed low, 31.4% to 28.6% [3274]; the template often went unused. Allergies fell from 27.5% to 3.3% and useful links stayed at 13.3% [3246].
consultant_advice: Letters score well on diagnosis, medication and timeliness, so don't re-audit those. Measure what the GP needs: a clear action for the GP, allergies and physical health. Then check whether the template is actually used.
